rationale:
Split into 12 children: 3 new lemmas plus 9 reused comparator-accepted declarations.

Why split. The supplied proof has two parts:
(i) an analytic part (Lemma 1 locality, Lemma 2 weights, Corollary 3), showing that weighted approximate tangent planes of two carriers agree a.e. on their overlap;
(ii) bookkeeping (Steps 4–8): frame sign, signed multiplicity s, M = {s ≠ 0}, θ = |s|, ξ = sign(s)ξ_i, Z = τ(M,θ,ξ) and the triple conditions.
Part (ii) is exactly the accepted `fiw_ims_combine` applied to the two-term coefficient sequence (a, b, 0, 0, …). That theorem says an integer series of integer rectifiable triples is one such triple (steps 5–9 of the supplied proof of Simon 3.13), and it is already proved in Lean and passed its comparator, so it is reused. Its only hypothesis is the tangent comparison principle (TO) on U = ℝ^N for all positive multiplicities. (TO) is the new child `tangent_overlap`, which carries part (i). Lemmas 1 and 2 become the reusable new children `subset_locality` and `weight_change`.

How the supplied proof maps onto the children:
- Lemma 1, weighted half → `subset_locality`.
  · Same Upper Density Theorem argument, run through the reused `zero_density_off_set` (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6/3.7(2)) and `tangent_locality` (equal blow-up limits when r^{-k}∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)}|1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′| → 0).
  · The weighted form needs no local finiteness of Hᵏ⌞E′.
- Lemma 2 → `weight_change`: on E with Hᵏ⌞E locally finite, HasWATS(E,θ) ⇒ HasWATS(E,θ′) a.e.
  · With θ′ ≡ 1 or θ ≡ 1 this is Lemma 2 (weight 1 is Definition 1.4).
  · Deviation: the proof uses normalized Lebesgue points (reused `lebesgue_points`), homogeneity of Definition 1.7 and `tangent_locality`, instead of Lusin compact pieces. Same hypotheses, much shorter Lean route.
- Corollary 3 and the transfer chains of Steps 4 and 7 → `tangent_overlap`: a.e. on M₁ ∩ M₂, HasWATS(M₁,θ₁,x,Q) ⇒ HasWATS(M₂,θ₂,x,Q), via subset_locality, weight_change, subset_locality.
  · `fiw_ims_combine` needs (TO) for every positive multiplicity, while Lemma 2 needs local finiteness. So the overlap is cut into E_j = {θ₁, θ₂ ≥ 1/(j+1)}, as with the compact pieces of Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1); local finiteness on E_j is Chebyshev.
- Step 4 (ξ₂ = ±ξ₁ a.e. on the overlap) → reused `orientation_sign` (with `frame_sign`), used inside `fiw_ims_combine` with (TO).
- Steps 5–8 → reused `im_combine`, with (M_r,θ_r,ξ_r) = (M₁,θ₁,ξ₁) for r = 0, (M₂,θ₂,ξ₂) for r ≥ 1, and c = (a, b, 0, …).
  · Its proof forms θ̂ = Σ_r c_r σ_r θ_r 1_{M_r} against the first-index orientation ξ̂, then M′ = {θ̂ ≠ 0}, θ′ = |θ̂|, ξ′ = sign(θ̂)ξ̂. These agree H-a.e. with the supplied s, M, θ, ξ (ε = σ₂ on M₁ ∩ M₂ when a ≠ 0; if a = 0 the reference orientation is ξ₂), since `fiw_ims_combine` takes the first index only over {c_r ≠ 0} and removes a null set.
  · Its step 10 proves the triple conditions, with the orientation of M′ obtained from (TO) for (M_r,θ_r) versus (M′,θ′), exactly as in the supplied Step 7.
  · Finite overlap and the HasSum come from the reused `overlap_finite` and `tsum_tau`.
- Preliminaries need no separate child. The unit fact, local finiteness of Hᵏ⌞M_i, k > N and k = 0 are all handled inside the reused lemmas, which are uniform in k.

Its accepted natural-language proof follows verbatim.

Source: Simon, Ch. 1, Theorem 3.3 and its printed proof (p. 15) with A₁ := A and A₂ := V, using the 5-times covering lemma 3.4 and Corollary 3.5. (SimonGMT formalizes exactly this argument: mul_simonHausdorff_le_of_le_dimensionalUpperDensity, together with dimensionalUpperDensity_inter_of_mem_nhds and simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure.)

1. Normalizations. The outer measure of ν (ν(S) = inf{ν(B) : B ⊇ S Borel}) is Borel regular and all Borel sets are ν-measurable (Carathéodory), as required in 3.3. Simon's Hausdorff measure Hⁿ (covers by sets C of diameter < δ with cost ω_n (diam C/2)ⁿ, then δ ↓ 0) coincides with μHE[n] as an outer measure on ℝ^P: both are the n-dimensional Hausdorff measure normalized to agree with Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (Simon Ch. 1, 2.8-2.10; SimonGMT simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure). Write Θ*ⁿ(ν, V, x) := limsup_{r↓0} ν(V ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) (Simon (3.1)).

2. Localization. If x ∈ A ⊆ V and V is open, there is R > 0 with B̄_R(x) ⊆ V, so ν(V ∩ B̄_r(x)) = ν(B̄_r(x)) for 0 < r < R and Θ*ⁿ(ν, V, x) = Θ*ⁿ(ν, x) ≥ t. So the hypothesis of 3.3 holds with A₁ = A ⊆ A₂ = V.

3. Trivial cases. If t = 0 or ν(V) = ∞ there is nothing to prove. If t = ∞, then the hypothesis holds with every real t′ > 0 in place of t, so by the case 0 < t′ < ∞ below t′ Hⁿ(A) ≤ ν(V) for all such t′; hence either Hⁿ(A) = 0 (and ∞·0 = 0 ≤ ν(V)) or ν(V) = ∞. So assume 0 < t < ∞ and ν(V) < ∞.

4. Printed proof of 3.3. Take τ ∈ (0, t), so Θ*ⁿ(ν, V, x) > τ for every x ∈ A. For δ > 0 let 𝓑 be the family of closed balls B̄_ρ(x) with x ∈ A, 0 < ρ < δ/2 and ν(V ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≥ τ ω_n ρⁿ. By the definition of the limsup, 𝓑 covers A finely. By the 5-times covering lemma 3.4 there is a pairwise disjoint subfamily 𝓑′ ⊆ 𝓑 such that every B ∈ 𝓑 meets some B′ ∈ 𝓑′ with diam B′ ≥ diam B/2, hence B is contained in the concentric ball B̂′ with 5 times the radius of B′. Since ν(V ∩ B) > 0 for B ∈ 𝓑 and, for finitely many disjoint B_1, …, B_N ∈ 𝓑′, Σ_j ν(V ∩ B_j) = ν(V ∩ ⋃_j B_j) ≤ ν(V) < ∞, the family 𝓑′ is countable, 𝓑′ = {B̄_{ρ_j}(x_j) : j ≥ 1}, and Σ_j ω_n ρ_jⁿ ≤ τ^{-1} Σ_j ν(V ∩ B̄_{ρ_j}(x_j)) ≤ τ^{-1} ν(V) < ∞. By Corollary 3.5, A ∖ ⋃_{j ≤ N} B̄_{ρ_j}(x_j) ⊆ ⋃_{j > N} B̄_{5ρ_j}(x_j) for every N. These balls have diameter < 5δ and a ball of radius ρ has cost ω_n (diam/2)ⁿ ≤ ω_n ρⁿ, so by the definition of Hⁿ_{5δ}: Hⁿ_{5δ}(A) ≤ Σ_{j ≤ N} ω_n ρ_jⁿ + 5ⁿ Σ_{j > N} ω_n ρ_jⁿ. Letting N → ∞ (the tail of a convergent series tends to 0) gives Hⁿ_{5δ}(A) ≤ Σ_j ω_n ρ_jⁿ ≤ τ^{-1} ν(V).

5. Letting δ ↓ 0 gives τ Hⁿ(A) ≤ ν(V), and letting τ ↑ t gives t Hⁿ(A) ≤ ν(V). By step 1 this is t·μHE[n](A) ≤ ν(V). (For n = 0 the same argument applies with ω_0 = 1 and ρ⁰ = 1.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Identify Simon's Hⁿ with μHE[n] (outer measures) and use Borel regularity of ν.
For x ∈ A ⊆ V with V open, Θ*ⁿ(ν, V, x) = Θ*ⁿ(ν, x) ≥ t, so Theorem 3.3 applies with A₁ = A, A₂ = V.
Dispose of t ∈ {0, ∞} and ν(V) = ∞.
Fine cover of A by balls with ν(V ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≥ τω_nρⁿ; the 5-times covering lemma gives a countable disjoint subfamily with Σ ω_nρ_jⁿ ≤ τ⁻¹ν(V).
Corollary 3.5 bounds Hⁿ_{5δ}(A) by the subfamily's cost; let δ ↓ 0 and τ ↑ t.

Its frozen Lean type, prose statement and title are byte-identical to the comparator-accepted DAG node root.integrality_weak_limits-a1.tangent_locality-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 96e830881dafe74af53547d1e5de4de197719c25), declaration Submission.iwl_weighted_tangent_locality, which is reused rather than re-proved (no new worker). Its accepted natural-language proof follows verbatim.

Conventions (fixed for this proof). ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P. Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure (a positive constant multiple of μH[k]; it equals Lebesgue measure on a k-dimensional Euclidean space, and μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure). D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k; D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k (C^∞ k-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport contained in U). I(k,P) := the strictly increasing maps {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; for I ∈ I(k,P), e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}) and dx^I is the constant k-covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} (J ∈ I(k,P)); every k-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (the norm used in the definition of mass), and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a form ω. For a k-vector w (an element of NVector = the dual of the k-covectors) put w^I := w(dx^I) and |w|_* := (Σ_I (w^I)²)^{1/2}; then w(α) = Σ_I α(e_I) w^I, so |w(α)| ≤ |α| |w|_* (Cauchy–Schwarz). M_W(X) := X.massOn W, M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X), spt X := X.support, X_j ⇀ X := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary. τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) := tauAction = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ with ⟨ω,ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)); "i.m." := IsIntegerMultiplicity; "X⌞A" denotes a current S with IsRestriction X A S; W ⊂⊂ U := CompactlyContainedOpen W U. B_r(x), B̄_r(x) denote open and closed balls.

Source: this is the locality property of Simon's weighted approximate tangent spaces (Ch. 3, 1.7), used in the parent proof in (P4)(iv) ("the weighted approximate tangent space at x ∈ V_i depends only on M ∩ V_i and θ|V_i modulo Hᵏ-null sets (for small r the blow-up integrals only see x + r·spt f ⊆ V_i, and Hᵏ(η_{x,r}Z) = r^{−k}Hᵏ(Z) = 0 for null Z)") and in the same way in Steps 2, 11 and (P5). Here it is stated and proved in the quantitative form needed by all those uses.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n] with a constant c_n ∈ (0,∞). η_{x,r}(y) := blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹(y − x). Recall the definition: HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q means dim Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P,ℝ), I_{M,θ}(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y) θ(x + r y) dHⁿ(y) → θ(x) ∫_Q f dHⁿ as r → 0, r > 0.

1. (Change of variables under the blow-up.) Fix r > 0. The map η_{x,r} is an affine bijection of ℝ^P (a translation followed by the dilation by r⁻¹) with inverse z ↦ x + r z, and for every set A ⊆ ℝ^P, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n} Hⁿ(A): Hausdorff measure is translation invariant and scales by λⁿ under the dilation y ↦ λy (Mathlib `hausdorffMeasure_smul`, `hausdorffMeasure_smul_right_image`; the constant c_n does not matter). Equivalently, the push-forward of Hⁿ⌞A under the measurable equivalence η_{x,r} is rⁿ·Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(A). Hence, for every g : ℝ^P → ℝ,
   ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} g dHⁿ = r^{−n} ∫_A g(η_{x,r}(z)) dHⁿ(z),
   both sides being integrable or not simultaneously (change of variables under a measurable equivalence that multiplies the measure by a constant; with the Bochner convention both sides are 0 in the non-integrable case).
2. Applying step 1 with A = M and g(y) := f(y) θ(x + r y), and using x + r·η_{x,r}(z) = z, we get for every r > 0
   I_{M,θ}(r) = r^{−n} ∫_M f(η_{x,r}(z)) θ(z) dHⁿ(z) = r^{−n} ∫ f(η_{x,r}(z)) (1_M θ)(z) dHⁿ(z),
   and the same formula for (M′, θ′). The second equality (integral over M = integral of the indicator) uses that M is Hⁿ-null-measurable (Mathlib `integral_indicator₀`); this hypothesis is essential: for a non-measurable M (e.g. a Bernstein set) the restricted measure Hⁿ⌞M and the lower integral of 1_M can disagree, and the statement would fail.
3. The dimension conditions dim Q = n in the two definitions are identical, so it remains to compare the limits. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P,ℝ), choose R ≥ 1 with spt f ⊆ B̄_R(0), and let ‖f‖_∞ := sup|f|. Let ρ > 0 be as in the hypothesis. For 0 < r < ρ/R: f(η_{x,r}(z)) ≠ 0 implies |z − x| ≤ R r < ρ, so the integrand of step 2 vanishes outside B̄_ρ(x); on M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) it is the product of the bounded continuous function f∘η_{x,r} with θ, which is Hⁿ-integrable there by hypothesis. Since M is null-measurable, 1_Mθ is a.e.-strongly measurable on B̄_ρ(x) (`AEStronglyMeasurable.indicator₀`), so the integrand is integrable; likewise for (M′,θ′). In particular |1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′| is a.e.-measurable on B̄_ρ(x), so its lower integral below is a genuine integral.
4. Consequently, for 0 < r < ρ/R,
   |I_{M,θ}(r) − I_{M′,θ′}(r)| = r^{−n} |∫ f(η_{x,r}(z)) (1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′)(z) dHⁿ(z)| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ r^{−n} ∫_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} |1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′| dHⁿ,
   because |f∘η_{x,r}| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ · 1_{B̄_{Rr}(x)}. By hypothesis (applied with this R) the right side tends to 0 as r ↓ 0 (in ℝ≥0∞, hence eventually finite and then tending to 0 as real numbers). So I_{M,θ}(r) − I_{M′,θ′}(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺.

Conventions: ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) = Eucl P with norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure, = μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)); on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume (`EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`). B̄_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ. η_{y,λ}(x) = λ⁻¹(x − y) is `Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap y λ`. ∫_A f dHⁿ is the Bochner set integral (0 when f is not integrable on A); ∫⁻ is the [0,∞]-valued lintegral. This is item 0(f) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6, Upper Density Theorem), in the localized form used in steps 2(i), 2(ii) and 3 of the parent proof. Let μ := μHE[n] on ℝ^Q.

1. (The measure ν.) Let ν := (μ⌞S).withDensity(g), a Borel measure on ℝ^Q (no measurability of g or S is needed to form it). For every Borel set E, ν(E) = ∫⁻_E g d(μ⌞S) = ∫⁻_{S ∩ E} g dμ (`withDensity_apply`, `Measure.restrict_restrict`). In particular ν(B̄_ρ(y)) = ∫⁻_{S ∩ B̄_ρ(y)} g dμ for all y, ρ, and ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W.

2. (Measurable hull.) Since S is μ-null-measurable there is a Borel set S′ ⊇ S with μ(S′ ∖ S) = 0 (e.g. S′ := toMeasurable μ S). ν is concentrated on S′: if E is Borel with E ∩ S′ = ∅ then S ∩ E = ∅, so ν(E) = 0; hence ν(E) = ν(E ∩ S′) for every Borel E.

3. (Countable compact family.) Let D ⊆ ℝ^Q be countable and dense, and 𝒦 the countable family of closed balls B̄_{2t}(q) ⊆ W with q ∈ D and t ∈ ℚ, t > 0. Every y ∈ W lies in the interior of some K ∈ 𝒦: choose rational t > 0 with B̄_{3t}(y) ⊆ W and q ∈ D with |q − y| < t; then y ∈ B_{2t}(q) ⊆ interior B̄_{2t}(q) and B̄_{2t}(q) ⊆ B̄_{3t}(y) ⊆ W. Each K ∈ 𝒦 is compact and K ⊆ W, so ν(K) < ∞.

4. (Upper Density Theorem.) ν̂ := ν.toOuterMeasure is Borel regular in Simon's sense (SimonGMT `Chapter01.measure_toOuterMeasure_isBorelRegular`). For K ∈ 𝒦 the set A_K := S′ ∩ K is Borel, hence ν̂-Carathéodory measurable, and ν̂(A_K) ≤ ν(K) < ∞. Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 (SimonGMT `Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6`, or its a.e. form `Chapter01.ae_dimensionalUpperDensity_eq_zero_outside`, Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean, with real dimension n ≥ 0) states that for Simon-Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ A_K,
 Θ*ⁿ(ν̂, A_K, x) = limsup_{ρ↓0} ν̂(A_K ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) / (ω_n · ofReal(ρ)ⁿ) = 0, where ω_n = realUnitBallVolume n ∈ (0, ∞).
 Simon's Hausdorff measure `simonHausdorffMeasureReal n` equals μHE[n] (SimonGMT `Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure`), so the exceptional set E_K := {x ∉ A_K : Θ*ⁿ(ν̂, A_K, x) ≠ 0} is μ-null.

5. (A good point.) Let Z := (S′ ∖ S) ∪ ⋃_{K∈𝒦} E_K, a countable union of μ-null sets, so μ(Z) = 0. Let y ∈ W with y ∉ S and y ∉ Z. Then y ∉ S′. Choose K ∈ 𝒦 with y ∈ interior K (step 3); then y ∉ A_K and y ∉ E_K, so limsup_{ρ↓0} ν(A_K ∩ B̄_ρ(y))/(ω_n ofReal(ρ)ⁿ) = 0 (ν̂ = ν on Borel sets). For ρ > 0 so small that B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ K we have A_K ∩ B̄_ρ(y) = S′ ∩ B̄_ρ(y), and ν(S′ ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) = ν(B̄_ρ(y)) by step 2.

6. (Conclusion.) Hence the [0, ∞]-valued function ρ ↦ ν(B̄_ρ(y))/(ω_n ofReal(ρ)ⁿ) has limsup 0 as ρ → 0+, so it tends to 0 (it is ≥ 0). Since the SimonGMT quotient uses ofReal(ρ)^(n : ℝ) = ofReal(ρ)ⁿ (`ENNReal.rpow_natCast`), ofReal(ρⁿ) = ofReal(ρ)ⁿ for ρ ≥ 0 (`ENNReal.ofReal_pow`), and ω_n is finite, ν(B̄_ρ(y))/ofReal(ρⁿ) = ω_n · [ν(B̄_ρ(y))/(ω_n ofReal(ρ)ⁿ)] → ω_n · 0 = 0. By step 1, ν(B̄_ρ(y)) = ∫⁻_{S∩B̄_ρ(y)} g dμ. This holds for every y ∈ W ∖ (S ∪ Z), i.e. for μ-a.e. y with y ∈ W and y ∉ S. ∎ (For n = 0 the same argument applies; then μ-null sets are empty and the statement says ν(B̄_ρ(y)) → ν({y}) = 0 for every y ∈ W ∖ S.)

Apply Simon's Upper Density Theorem 3.6 (SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_6) to ν̂ = ν.toOuterMeasure (Borel regular) and A_K = S′ ∩ K; Simon's Hⁿ equals μHE[n], so exceptional sets are Hⁿ-null.
At y ∈ W∖(S ∪ null set), localize to B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ K: ν(A_K ∩ B̄_ρ(y)) = ν(B̄_ρ(y)), so the density quotient tends to 0; rescale by ω_n.

Source. This combines preliminary (v) and property (G2) of the parent proof: normalized Lebesgue points via the Lebesgue–Besicovitch differentiation theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.23 with the Symmetric Vitali Property 3.11(3); Mathlib's Besicovitch Vitali family), with Θ*ᵏ < ∞. Finiteness of the upper density is obtained from the sibling `rectifiability_density_comparison` (Simon Ch. 1, 3.3: if V is open, A ⊆ V and t ≤ Θ*ᵏ(λ, x) on A, then t·H(A) ≤ λ(V)). This replaces the tangent-plane argument (vi) of the parent proof and needs no tangent plane.

Statement. Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and M ⊆ U be H-null-measurable, with H(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be H-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U. Then for H⌞M-a.e. x and every R > 0:
  r^{−k} ∫⁻_{M ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖f(y) − f(x)‖ₑ dH(y) → 0 as r ↓ 0.

1. (Countable cover by relatively compact balls.)
   - If U = ∅ then M = ∅ and H⌞M = 0, so there is nothing to prove.
   - The balls B_s(y) with s > 0 and B̄_s(y) ⊆ U cover U. By second countability of ℝ^P, countably many of them, W_i := B_{s_i}(y_i) (i ∈ ℕ), cover U (`TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable`).
   - K_i := B̄_{s_i}(y_i) is compact with W_i ⊆ K_i ⊆ U.
   - Since M ⊆ U = ⋃_i W_i, and a countable union of H⌞M-null sets is H⌞M-null, it suffices to fix i and prove the claim for H⌞M-a.e. x ∈ W_i. Write W := W_i and K := K_i.

2. (A finite measure.)
   - λ := H⌞(M ∩ K) is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, since λ(ℝ^P) = H(M ∩ K) < ∞.
   - f is λ-integrable, by the hypothesis with this K.
   - For x ∈ W and s > 0 with B̄_s(x) ⊆ W ⊆ K: λ(B̄_s(x)) = H(M ∩ B̄_s(x)), and ∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖f − f(x)‖ₑ dλ = ∫⁻_{M ∩ B̄_s(x)} ‖f − f(x)‖ₑ dH. Here λ⌞B̄_s(x) = H⌞(B̄_s(x) ∩ M ∩ K) by `Measure.restrict_restrict` (closed balls are measurable), and B̄_s(x) ∩ M ∩ K = M ∩ B̄_s(x).

3. (Lebesgue–Besicovitch differentiation.)
   - λ is finite, hence locally finite and s-finite, and ℝ^P has the Besicovitch covering property (finite-dimensional normed space).
   - Apply Mathlib's `VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div` to the Vitali family `Besicovitch.vitaliFamily λ` and the λ-integrable (hence locally integrable) f. Compose with `Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt λ x`: closed balls B̄_s(x), s ↓ 0, tend to the Vitali filter at x.
   - This gives a λ-null set N such that for every x ∉ N:
     a_x(s) := (∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖f − f(x)‖ₑ dλ) / λ(B̄_s(x)) → 0 as s ↓ 0.
   - λ(N) = 0 means H(N ∩ M ∩ K) = 0, since M ∩ K is null-measurable (`Measure.restrict_apply₀'`). Hence H⌞M(N ∩ W) = 0.

4. (Finite upper density.)
   - Let A_∞ := {x ∈ W : Θ*ᵏ(λ, x) = ∞}.
   - For every real t > 0: A_∞ ⊆ W, W is open, and t ≤ Θ*ᵏ(λ, x) for x ∈ A_∞. The sibling `rectifiability_density_comparison` gives t·H(A_∞) ≤ λ(W) ≤ λ(ℝ^P) < ∞.
   - If H(A_∞) > 0, then t·H(A_∞) > λ(ℝ^P) for all large real t (also when H(A_∞) = ∞), a contradiction. So H(A_∞) = 0, hence H⌞M(A_∞) = 0.

5. (Good points.) Let x ∈ M ∩ W with x ∉ N ∪ A_∞, and fix R > 0.
   - Θ*ᵏ(λ, x) < ∞, so choose a real C > 0 with Θ*ᵏ(λ, x) < C. By the definition of limsup (`Filter.eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt`), eventually for s ↓ 0, λ(B̄_s(x))/(ω_k s^k) < C, i.e. λ(B̄_s(x)) ≤ C ω_k s^k.
   - Since Rr ↓ 0 as r ↓ 0 and W is open, for all sufficiently small r > 0 the radius s := Rr satisfies both this bound and B̄_s(x) ⊆ W.
   - For such r, put I(r) := ∫⁻_{M ∩ B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖f − f(x)‖ₑ dH = ∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖f − f(x)‖ₑ dλ (step 2). Then I(r) ≤ λ(B̄_s(x)) · a_x(s):
     · if 0 < λ(B̄_s(x)) < ∞, this is an equality by the definition of a_x(s) (`ENNReal.div_mul_cancel`);
     · if λ(B̄_s(x)) = 0, then λ⌞B̄_s(x) = 0 and I(r) = 0.
   - Therefore r^{−k} I(r) ≤ r^{−k} · C ω_k (Rr)^k · a_x(Rr) = (C ω_k R^k) · a_x(Rr).
   - The right side tends to (C ω_k R^k) · 0 = 0 as r ↓ 0. This is step 3 composed with r ↦ Rr, which maps 𝓝[>] 0 to 𝓝[>] 0, together with `ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul`, using C ω_k R^k ≠ ∞.
   - By the squeeze theorem in [0, ∞] (`tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le'`, lower bound 0), r^{−k} I(r) → 0.

6. (Conclusion.) By steps 3–4, H⌞M-a.e. x ∈ W is a good point in the sense of step 5. By step 1 the claim holds for H⌞M-a.e. x. ∎

subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P be orthonormal families with span(range τ) = span(range τ'). Then simpleNVector τ' = simpleNVector τ or simpleNVector τ' = −simpleNVector τ.

Reused accepted declaration. Its frozen Lean type, prose statement and title are byte-identical to the comparator-accepted DAG node root.flat_iff_weak-a1.im_series-a1.frame_sign-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit c90a40505abdbff33b9174acf9b20037eb2cb2a1), declaration Submission.fiw_ims_frame_sign, which is reused rather than re-proved (no new worker). Its accepted natural-language proof follows verbatim.

1. (Two orthonormal bases of Q.) Let Q := span(range τ) = span(range τ').
   - An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so τ is a basis of Q (Basis.span).
   - It is orthonormal for the inner product of Q, which is the ambient one. Call this orthonormal basis b of Q (Basis.toOrthonormalBasis).
   - In the same way τ' is an orthonormal basis of span(range τ') = Q. Transporting along this equality of submodules gives an orthonormal basis b' of Q with b'_j = τ'_j.
   - In particular dim Q = n.

2. (Change of frame.) Let α be any n-covector on ℝ^P.
   - Its restriction f := α ∘ (inclusion Q ↪ ℝ^P), f(v_1, …, v_n) := α(v_1, …, v_n), is an alternating n-linear form on the n-dimensional space Q (AlternatingMap.compLinearMap with Q.subtype).
   - By AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det, f = f(b)·b.det.
   - Evaluating at b': α(τ') = f(b') = f(b)·b.det(b') = d·α(τ), where d := b.det(b') does not depend on α.
   - Elementary version: τ'_j = Σ_i O_{ij} τ_i with O_{ij} = ⟨τ_i, τ'_j⟩, because τ'_j ∈ Q and τ is an orthonormal basis of Q. Multilinearity and alternation give α(τ') = det(O)·α(τ), and d = det O.

3. (d = ±1.) b.det(b') is the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix between the orthonormal bases b and b' of Q. That matrix is orthogonal, so d = 1 or d = −1 (OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real). Elementary version: OᵀO = I because τ' is orthonormal, so d² = 1.

4. (Conclusion.)
   - For every α: (simpleNVector τ')(α) = α(τ') = d·α(τ) = (d • simpleNVector τ)(α) (simpleNVector_apply).
   - By extensionality of continuous linear maps, simpleNVector τ' = d • simpleNVector τ. This is simpleNVector τ if d = 1 and −simpleNVector τ if d = −1.
   - For n = 0 both families are empty, Q = 0, d = 1, and both sides are evaluation at the empty tuple. ∎
proof_key_steps: τ and τ' are orthonormal bases of the same n-dimensional subspace Q
restrict α to Q: α(τ') = b.det(b')·α(τ) by AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det
b.det(b') = ±1 since the change of basis between orthonormal bases is orthogonal

Then for H-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂, ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x) or ξ₁(x) = −ξ₂(x).

Let μ := H.restrict(M₁ ∩ M₂) and s(τ) := simpleNVector τ.

1. (Points of the overlap.) M₁ ∩ M₂ is H-null-measurable (field nullMeasurableSet of both triples, NullMeasurableSet.inter). So μ-a.e. x lies in M₁ ∩ M₂ (ae_restrict_mem₀). For such x, x ∈ M₂, so θ₂(x) > 0 (field pos of the second triple); in particular θ₂(x) ≠ 0.

2. (Frames from both orientation conditions.)
   - The field orients of the first triple holds H.restrict M₁-a.e., hence μ-a.e. because M₁ ∩ M₂ ⊆ M₁ (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). It gives an orthonormal τ¹ : Fin n → ℝ^P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₁ θ₁ x (span(range τ¹)) and ξ₁(x) = s(τ¹) or ξ₁(x) = −s(τ¹).
   - Likewise, using M₁ ∩ M₂ ⊆ M₂, μ-a.e. there is an orthonormal τ² with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M₂ θ₂ x (span(range τ²)) and ξ₂(x) = ±s(τ²).

3. (Equal spans.)
   - Intersect the μ-a.e. statements of steps 1–2 with the hypothesis (filter_upwards), and fix such an x.
   - The hypothesis with Q := span(range τ¹) shows that span(range τ¹) is also a weighted approximate tangent space of (M₂, θ₂) at x.
   - Since θ₂(x) ≠ 0, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique gives span(range τ¹) = span(range τ²).

4. (Combine the signs.)
   - The sibling frame_sign with τ := τ¹, τ' := τ² gives s(τ²) = ε·s(τ¹) with ε ∈ {1, −1}.
   - Write ξ₁(x) = ε₁·s(τ¹) and ξ₂(x) = ε₂·s(τ²) with ε₁, ε₂ ∈ {1, −1}.
   - Then ξ₂(x) = ε₂ε·s(τ¹), so s(τ¹) = ε₂ε·ξ₂(x) because (ε₂ε)² = 1.
   - Hence ξ₁(x) = ε₁ε₂ε·ξ₂(x) with ε₁ε₂ε ∈ {1, −1}, i.e. ξ₁(x) = ξ₂(x) or ξ₁(x) = −ξ₂(x). This is an eight-case check using neg_neg. ∎

Notation: |c_r| := ((c_r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) and g_r := |c_r|·1_{M_r}·ofReal θ_r, so Θ = Σ'_r g_r.

1. (Measurability.) Fix W with CompactlyContainedOpen W U and fix r.
   - closure W is a compact subset of U, so θ_r is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, on M_r ∩ closure W, and therefore on M_r ∩ W.
   - W is open, hence measurable, so (H.restrict W).restrict M_r = H.restrict(M_r ∩ W) (Measure.restrict_restrict'). Also M_r is null-measurable for H.restrict W.
   - By aemeasurable_indicator_iff₀, 1_{M_r}·ofReal θ_r, and hence g_r, is AEMeasurable for H.restrict W.
   - So is Θ (AEMeasurable.ennreal_tsum).

2. (Integral over W.) By lintegral_tsum (using step 1), lintegral_const_mul' (|c_r| < ∞) and lintegral_indicator₀:
   ∫⁻_W Θ dH = Σ'_r |c_r|·∫⁻_W 1_{M_r}·ofReal θ_r dH = Σ'_r |c_r|·∫⁻_{M_r ∩ W} ofReal θ_r dH < ∞, by hypothesis.

3. (Conclusion (a).) Let K ⊆ U be compact.
   - ℝ^P is locally compact and regular, so exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure gives an open W with K ⊆ W, closure W ⊆ U and closure W compact, i.e. CompactlyContainedOpen W U.
   - By lintegral_mono_set and step 2, ∫⁻_K Θ dH ≤ ∫⁻_W Θ dH < ∞.

4. (Θ < ∞ a.e. on U.) Let N := {x ∈ U : Θ(x) = ∞}.
   - For x ∈ N, the construction of step 3 with K := {x} gives W_x ⊂⊂ U with x ∈ W_x.
   - By steps 1–2, Θ is AEMeasurable for H.restrict W_x and has finite integral there, so Θ < ∞ H.restrict W_x-a.e. (ae_lt_top').
   - W_x is measurable, so ae_restrict_iff' gives H({y ∈ W_x : Θ(y) = ∞}) = 0, hence H(N ∩ W_x) = 0.
   - W_x is an open neighbourhood of x, so N ∩ W_x ∈ 𝓝[N] x.
   - ℝ^P is second countable, so measure_null_of_locally_null gives H(N) = 0.

5. (Conclusion (b).) Let x ∉ N and F(x) := {r : c_r ≠ 0, x ∈ M_r}.
   - If x ∉ U, then x ∉ M_r for every r (M_r ⊆ U), so F(x) = ∅.
   - If x ∈ U, then Θ(x) < ∞. For r ∈ F(x), |c_r| ≥ 1 (a nonzero integer) and 1_{M_r}(x)·ofReal θ_r(x) = ofReal θ_r(x) ≥ 1, so g_r(x) ≥ 1.
   - If F(x) were infinite, then for every m ∈ ℕ it would contain a finite subset F_m with m elements (Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq). Then Θ(x) ≥ Σ_{r∈F_m} g_r(x) ≥ m for every m (ENNReal.sum_le_tsum), contradicting Θ(x) < ∞.
   - Hence F(x) is finite for every x ∉ N. Since H(N) = 0, F(x) is finite for H-a.e. x. ∎

   - ω is continuous (smooth) and vanishes off the compact set K. So there is B ≥ 0 with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B for all x, and ω(x) = 0 for x ∉ K.

2. (Unit bound.)
   - If τ is orthonormal and α is an n-covector, then |s(τ)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ (simpleNVector_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm, ‖τ_i‖ = 1). The same holds for −s(τ).

   |F_r(x)| ≤ |c_r|·B·1_{M_r ∩ W}(x)·θ_r(x)   (using K ⊆ W).

   - On M_r ∩ L:
     • θ_r is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable (L is compact and L ⊆ U);
     • ξ_r is a.e.-strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable, restricted from M_r to M_r ∩ L);
     • ω is continuous;
     • the evaluation (v, α) ↦ v(α), NVector × Covector → ℝ, is continuous (bounded bilinear).
   - Hence x ↦ ξ_r(x)(ω(x)) and g_r are a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict(M_r ∩ L).
   - So F_r is a.e.-strongly measurable for H (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff₀; M_r ∩ L is null-measurable).

The curried ContinuousLinearMap.apply route fails, because no TopologicalSpace instance is found on `NVector (Eucl P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ`.

   - By step 3, lintegral_mono_ae and lintegral_indicator₀: ∫⁻ ‖F_r‖ₑ dH ≤ |c_r|·ofReal B·∫⁻_{M_r ∩ W} ofReal θ_r dH.
   - So Σ'_r ∫⁻ ‖F_r‖ₑ dH ≤ ofReal B·A < ∞ (ENNReal.tsum_mul_left).
   - In particular every F_r is integrable (step 4 plus finite integral), and r ↦ ∫ |F_r| dH is summable.

6. (Termwise integration.) By hasSum_integral_of_summable_integral_norm (or integral_tsum together with step 5):
   HasSum (r ↦ ∫ F_r dH) (∫ Σ'_r F_r dH).

7. (Identification of the terms.) By integral_indicator₀ (M_r null-measurable) and integral_const_mul:
   ∫ F_r dH = ∫_{M_r} c_r·(θ_r(x)·ξ_r(x)(ω(x))) dH = c_r·∫_{M_r} θ_r(x)·ξ_r(x)(ω(x)) dH = c_r·tauAction n M_r θ_r ξ_r ω   (definition of tauAction).
   Substituting into step 6 proves the claim. ∎

This is steps 5–9 of the supplied proof of Simon 3.13 for M-absolutely convergent series.

Notation:
- I := {r : c_r ≠ 0}; |c_r| := ((c_r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞); s(τ) := simpleNVector τ.
- 'null' means H-null; hTL is the tangent-locality hypothesis.
- For x ∈ M_r, θ_r(x) ∈ ℕ and θ_r(x) > 0 (field pos), so θ_r(x) ≥ 1.

Lean note (checked at this pin): instance search finds no PseudoMetrizableSpace, MetrizableSpace or ContinuousAdd on `NVector (Eucl P) n`.
- A local PseudoMetrizableSpace instance compiles:
  `letI u : UniformSpace (NVector (Eucl P) n) := PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace; haveI : (uniformity (NVector (Eucl P) n)).IsCountablyGenerated := @EMetric.instIsCountablyGeneratedUniformity _ PseudoMetricSpace.toPseudoEMetricSpace; exact @UniformSpace.pseudoMetrizableSpace _ u this`
- After that, MetrizableSpace is found by infer_instance, and aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff, StronglyMeasurable.measurableSet_eq_fun and aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae apply to NVector-valued maps.
- The construction below never adds NVector-valued functions. It only glues, restricts, multiplies by real functions (AEStronglyMeasurable.smul) and takes indicators (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff₀); all of these work as is.

1. (Exceptional null sets.)
   (a) The sibling overlap_finite applies. Its hypotheses are the fields subset, nullMeasurableSet and integrableOn of the triples, θ_r ≥ 1 on M_r, and the summability hypothesis. It gives:
       - Θ := Σ'_r |c_r|·1_{M_r}·ofReal θ_r satisfies ∫⁻_K Θ dH < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U;
       - there is a null set N_fin such that F(x) := {r ∈ I : x ∈ M_r} is finite for x ∉ N_fin.
   (b) For each r, the field orients and ae_restrict_iff'₀ (M_r null-measurable) give a null set N_r with the following property: for every x ∈ M_r ∖ N_r there is an orthonormal τ with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_r θ_r x (span(range τ)) and ξ_r(x) = ±s(τ).
   (c) For each r, r', hTL applied to (M_r, θ_r) and (M_{r'}, θ_{r'}) is exactly the locality hypothesis of the sibling orientation_sign. The hypotheses of hTL are the fields subset, nullMeasurableSet, pos and integrableOn of the two triples. orientation_sign then gives a null set N_{r,r'} with ξ_r(x) = ±ξ_{r'}(x) for x ∈ (M_r ∩ M_{r'}) ∖ N_{r,r'}.
   Let N₀ := toMeasurable H (N_fin ∪ ⋃_r N_r ∪ ⋃_{r,r'} N_{r,r'}). It is a measurable null set containing all of these, because countable unions of null sets are null. Put G := ℝ^P ∖ N₀; G is measurable and H(N₀) = 0.

2. (Union and first index.)
   - M_∪ := ⋃_{r∈I} M_r ⊆ U is null-measurable.
   - For x ∈ M_∪ let r(x) := min{r ∈ I : x ∈ M_r} (Nat.find).
   - For r ∈ I put A_r := M_r ∖ ⋃_{r'∈I, r'<r} M_{r'}, and A_r := ∅ for r ∉ I.
   - Then A_r = {x ∈ M_∪ : r(x) = r}, each A_r is null-measurable (a finite Boolean combination), and M_∪ = ⋃_r A_r.

3. (Reference orientation.)
   - Define ξ̂(x) := ξ_{r(x)}(x) for x ∈ M_∪ and ξ̂(x) := 0 otherwise. On A_r, ξ̂ = ξ_r.
   - ξ_r is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M_r, hence for H.restrict A_r (A_r ⊆ M_r).
   - Since ξ̂ = ξ_r on the null-measurable set A_r, ξ̂ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict A_r (AEStronglyMeasurable.congr with ae_restrict_mem₀).
   - By aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff (countable cover M_∪ = ⋃_r A_r), ξ̂ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M_∪.

4. (Signs.) For r ∈ ℕ and x ∈ ℝ^P let σ_r(x) := 1 if ξ_r(x) = ξ̂(x), and σ_r(x) := −1 otherwise.
   - Let r ∈ I and x ∈ G ∩ M_r. Then x ∈ M_∪, r(x) ∈ I and x ∈ (M_r ∩ M_{r(x)}) ∖ N_{r,r(x)}, so ξ_r(x) = ±ξ̂(x) by 1(c).
   - In both cases ξ_r(x) = σ_r(x)·ξ̂(x): if ξ_r(x) ≠ ξ̂(x), then ξ_r(x) = −ξ̂(x) and σ_r(x) = −1.
   - Measurability: for r ∈ I, ξ_r and ξ̂ are a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M_r (as M_r ⊆ M_∪). Replacing them by strongly measurable versions changes {ξ_r = ξ̂} only by a null set, and the equality set of the versions is measurable (StronglyMeasurable.measurableSet_eq_fun). So σ_r is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M_r.

5. (θ_r is measurable on M_r.)
   - U is σ-compact: an open subset of ℝ^P is a locally compact second-countable space, so IsSigmaCompact U. Explicitly, U = ⋃_j K_j with K_j := {x ∈ U : |x| ≤ j, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/j}, or K_j := closedBall 0 j if U = ℝ^P.
   - So M_r = ⋃_j (M_r ∩ K_j), and θ_r is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, on each M_r ∩ K_j.
   - By aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff, θ_r is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M_r.

6. (Integer multiplicity θ̂.) Let t_r := 1_{M_r}·(c_r·σ_r·θ_r), so t_r = 0 if r ∉ I, and let θ̂(x) := Σ'_r t_r(x) (a real tsum).
   - Each t_r is a.e.-strongly measurable for H (steps 4–5 and aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff₀).
   - For x ∈ G, t_r(x) = 0 for r ∉ F(x), which is a finite set. So θ̂(x) = Σ_{r∈F(x)} c_r·σ_r(x)·θ_r(x) (tsum_eq_sum) is a finite sum of integers, and θ̂(x) ∈ ℤ.
   - Moreover |θ̂(x)| ≤ Σ_{r∈F(x)} |c_r|·θ_r(x), hence ofReal|θ̂(x)| ≤ Σ_{r∈F(x)} |c_r|·ofReal θ_r(x) ≤ Θ(x) (ENNReal.sum_le_tsum).
   - For x ∈ G, the partial sums Σ_{r<N} t_r(x) equal θ̂(x) once N > max F(x). So they converge to θ̂ H-a.e., and θ̂ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H (aestronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto_ae).

7. (The new triple.) Define
   M' := {x ∈ M_∪ ∩ G : θ̂(x) ≠ 0},   θ' := 1_{M'}·|θ̂|,   ξ' := 1_{M'}·((θ̂/|θ̂|) • ξ̂).
   For x ∈ M':
   - θ̂(x)/|θ̂(x)| ∈ {1, −1};
   - θ'(x) = |θ̂(x)| = (θ̂(x)).natAbs ∈ ℕ by step 6, and θ'(x) > 0;
   - θ'(x)·ξ'(x) = θ̂(x)·ξ̂(x).

8. (Pointwise identity.) Fix ω ∈ D^n(U) and let F_r(x) := 1_{M_r}(x)·(c_r·(θ_r(x)·ξ_r(x)(ω(x)))), the integrand of the sibling tsum_tau. Let x ∈ G.
   - If x ∉ M_∪: every F_r(x) = 0 (either c_r = 0 or x ∉ M_r), and x ∉ M'. So Σ'_r F_r(x) = 0 = 1_{M'}(x)·θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω(x)).
   - If x ∈ M_∪: F_r(x) = 0 for r ∉ F(x), and F_r(x) = c_r·θ_r(x)·σ_r(x)·ξ̂(x)(ω(x)) for r ∈ F(x) by step 4. Hence Σ'_r F_r(x) = θ̂(x)·ξ̂(x)(ω(x)) (tsum of a finitely supported family, step 6).
     • If θ̂(x) ≠ 0, then x ∈ M' and this equals θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω(x)) (step 7).
     • If θ̂(x) = 0, then x ∉ M' and both sides are 0.
   So Σ'_r F_r = 1_{M'}·θ'·ξ'(ω) on G, i.e. H-a.e.

9. (HasSum.)
   - The sibling tsum_tau (same hypotheses) gives HasSum (r ↦ c_r·tauAction n M_r θ_r ξ_r ω) (∫ Σ'_r F_r dH).
   - By step 8 (integral_congr_ae) and integral_indicator₀ (M' is null-measurable, step 10(ii)):
     ∫ Σ'_r F_r dH = ∫_{M'} θ'(x)·ξ'(x)(ω(x)) dH = tauAction n M' θ' ξ' ω.

10. (Triple conditions for (M', θ', ξ').)
   (i) subset: M' ⊆ M_∪ ⊆ U.
   (ii) nullMeasurableSet: M' = M_∪ ∩ G ∩ {θ̂ ≠ 0}. M_∪ is null-measurable, G is measurable, and {θ̂ ≠ 0} is null-measurable because θ̂ is a.e.-measurable (step 6).
   (iii) countablyRectifiable: M' ⊆ M_∪ = ⋃_r M̃_r with M̃_r := M_r for r ∈ I and M̃_r := ∅ otherwise.
       - Each M̃_r is countably n-rectifiable: field countablyRectifiable, and ∅ via countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero.
       - Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_iUnion and CountablyRectifiable.mono give CountablyRectifiable n M'.
   (iv) pos, and θ' natural-valued on M': step 7.
   (v) integrableOn: let K ⊆ U be compact.
       - θ' is a.e.-strongly measurable (step 6, indicator of the null-measurable M') and θ' ≥ 0.
       - For x ∈ M' (⊆ G), ofReal θ'(x) = ofReal|θ̂(x)| ≤ Θ(x) (step 6).
       - So ∫⁻_{M'∩K} ofReal θ' dH ≤ ∫⁻_K Θ dH < ∞ (step 1(a)), and θ' is integrable on M' ∩ K.
   (vi) aestronglyMeasurable: θ̂/|θ̂| is a.e.-measurable (a quotient of a.e.-measurable real functions), and ξ̂ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M_∪, hence for H.restrict M'. So (θ̂/|θ̂|) • ξ̂ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H.restrict M', and so is ξ', which agrees with it on M'.
   (vii) orients:
       - For each r ∈ I apply hTL to (M_r, θ_r) and (M', θ'). Its hypotheses are the fields of the r-th triple together with (i), (ii), (iv), (v).
       - Via ae_restrict_iff'₀ (M_r ∩ M' null-measurable) this gives null sets N'_r such that, for x ∈ (M_r ∩ M') ∖ N'_r, every weighted approximate tangent space of (M_r, θ_r) at x is one of (M', θ') at x.
       - Let x ∈ M' ∖ ⋃_{r∈I} N'_r and r := r(x) ∈ I. Then x ∈ M_r and x ∈ G, so x ∉ N_r.
       - By 1(b) there is an orthonormal τ with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_r θ_r x (span(range τ)) and ξ_r(x) = ±s(τ).
       - As x ∈ (M_r ∩ M') ∖ N'_r, also HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' θ' x (span(range τ)).
       - Finally ξ'(x) = (θ̂(x)/|θ̂(x)|)·ξ̂(x) = ±ξ_r(x) = ±s(τ).
       - Since ⋃_{r∈I} N'_r is null, this holds for H.restrict M'-a.e. x (ae_restrict_iff'₀).
   Hence IsRectifiableTriple U n M' θ' ξ' holds. Together with step 7 (θ' natural-valued on M') and step 9, this proves the theorem. ∎
proof_key_steps: null sets: overlap_finite (finite overlaps, ∫_K Θ < ∞), the orientation conditions, and orientation_sign for all pairs (locality from hTL)
first-index reference orientation ξ̂ glued from ξ_r on A_r; signs σ_r with ξ_r = σ_r ξ̂ on M_r off the null set
θ̂ := Σ' 1_{M_r} c_r σ_r θ_r is an a.e.-measurable, integer-valued finite sum with |θ̂| ≤ Θ
tsum_tau gives HasSum with limit tauAction(M', θ', ξ')(ω)
triple conditions; orientation of M' via hTL applied to (M_r, θ_r) and (M', θ')

subproblems.title: Weighted approximate tangent spaces pass to and from a subset at almost every point of the subset
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ and H := μHE[k] on ℝ^N = Eucl N. Let E ⊆ M ⊆ ℝ^N be H-null-measurable sets and let θ : ℝ^N → ℝ be H-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N (no sign condition on θ and no local finiteness of H⌞M is assumed). Then for H-a.e. x ∈ E (that is, H⌞E-almost every x) and every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^N: Q is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.7 (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x Q: finrank Q = k and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dH(y) → θ(x)∫_Q f dH as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x)) if and only if Q is a weighted approximate tangent space of (E, θ) at x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (E M : Set (Eucl N)) (θ : Eucl N → ℝ), E ⊆ M → NullMeasurableSet E (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N)) → NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N)) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl N), IsCompact K → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N))) → ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N)).restrict E), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Eucl N), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x Q ↔ HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the weighted half of Lemma 1 (locality) of the parent proof, i.e. the Upper Density Theorem argument of Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2), as used in Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1). The density statement is the reused sibling zero_density_off_set (Submission.lpf_wtc_ae_zero_density_off_set, statement (ZD) below). The passage from vanishing density to equality of the two blow-up limits is the reused sibling tangent_locality (Submission.iwl_weighted_tangent_locality, statement (TL) below). Notation: ‖t‖ₑ = |t| ∈ [0, ∞) is the extended norm of t ∈ ℝ, B̄_ρ(x) := closedBall x ρ, r^{−k} means ENNReal.ofReal((r^k)⁻¹), and ρ^k in a denominator means ENNReal.ofReal(ρ^k).

(TL) [sibling tangent_locality]: for H-null-measurable M, M′ ⊆ ℝ^N, functions θ, θ′ and a point x with θ(x) = θ′(x), suppose that for some ρ > 0 θ is H-integrable on M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) and θ′ on M′ ∩ B̄_ρ(x), and that r^{−k}·∫⁻_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′‖ₑ dH → 0 as r ↓ 0 for every R > 0. Then for every linear subspace Q, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x Q ↔ HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M′ θ′ x Q.
(ZD) [sibling zero_density_off_set]: for W ⊆ ℝ^N open, S ⊆ ℝ^N H-null-measurable and g : ℝ^N → [0, ∞] with ∫⁻_{S∩K} g dH < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W: for H-a.e. y with y ∈ W and y ∉ S, (∫⁻_{S∩B̄_ρ(y)} g dH)/ρ^k → 0 in [0, ∞] as ρ ↓ 0.

1. (The excess set.) Put S := M ∖ E and g(z) := ‖θ(z)‖ₑ.
   - S is H-null-measurable, as a difference of null-measurable sets.
   - For compact K, S ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ K. So ∫⁻_{S∩K} g dH ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} ‖θ‖ₑ dH < ∞, because θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K (its norm has finite integral; lintegral_mono_set).

2. (Zero density at almost every point of E.)
   - Apply (ZD) with W := ℝ^N (open), S and g. Outside an H-null set, every y ∉ S has (∫⁻_{S∩B̄_ρ(y)} g dH)/ρ^k → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
   - An H-a.e. property also holds H⌞E-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae), and H⌞E-a.e. x lies in E (ae_restrict_mem₀, E null-measurable).
   - Since E ∩ S = ∅, for H⌞E-a.e. x we have x ∈ E and, writing I(ρ) := ∫⁻_{S∩B̄_ρ(x)} g dH, I(ρ)/ρ^k → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
   Fix such an x for the rest of the proof.

3. (Rescaling.) Let R > 0.
   - The map r ↦ Rr sends (0, ∞) into (0, ∞) and tends to 0 as r ↓ 0. Hence I(Rr)/(Rr)^k → 0 as r ↓ 0.
   - For r > 0, in [0, ∞]: r^{−k}·I(Rr) = R^k·(I(Rr)/(Rr)^k). Indeed ofReal(R^k)·ofReal(((Rr)^k)⁻¹) = ofReal(R^k·R^{−k}·r^{−k}) = ofReal((r^k)⁻¹) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos, mul_pow).
   - The finite constant R^k times a quantity tending to 0 tends to 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul). Therefore r^{−k}·I(Rr) → 0 as r ↓ 0.

4. (Identification of the integrand in (TL).)
   - Because E ⊆ M, for every z: 1_M(z)θ(z) − 1_E(z)θ(z) = 1_S(z)θ(z). Hence ‖1_Mθ(z) − 1_Eθ(z)‖ₑ = 1_S(z)·g(z). (Check the cases z ∈ E, z ∈ M ∖ E and z ∉ M.)
   - S is H-null-measurable, hence also null-measurable for H⌞B̄_ρ(x). So ∫⁻_{B̄_ρ(x)} ‖1_Mθ − 1_Eθ‖ₑ dH = ∫⁻_{B̄_ρ(x)} 1_S·g dH = ∫⁻_{S∩B̄_ρ(x)} g dH = I(ρ) (lintegral_indicator₀ and Measure.restrict_restrict₀).
   - With ρ = Rr, step 3 gives r^{−k}·∫⁻_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖1_Mθ − 1_Eθ‖ₑ dH → 0 as r ↓ 0, for every R > 0.

5. (Apply (TL).) Use (TL) with (M, θ), (M′, θ′) := (E, θ) and the point x:
   - M and E are H-null-measurable, and θ(x) = θ(x);
   - with ρ := 1, θ is integrable on M ∩ B̄_1(x) (B̄_1(x) is compact) and on E ∩ B̄_1(x) ⊆ M ∩ B̄_1(x) (IntegrableOn.mono_set);
   - the density hypothesis is step 4.
   Hence HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x Q ↔ HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q for every linear subspace Q. By step 2 this holds for H⌞E-a.e. x, which proves the lemma.
   For k = 0 every power r^k, ρ^k equals 1 and the same argument applies verbatim. ∎
proof_key_steps: S := M ∖ E is H-null-measurable and ‖θ‖ₑ has finite integral on S ∩ K for every compact K
zero_density_off_set with W = ℝ^N: ∫⁻_{S∩B̄_ρ(x)} ‖θ‖ₑ dH = o(ρ^k) for H⌞E-a.e. x, because E ∩ S = ∅
rescaling ρ = Rr: r^{−k}·∫⁻_{S∩B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖θ‖ₑ dH → 0 for every R > 0
E ⊆ M gives ‖1_Mθ − 1_Eθ‖ₑ = 1_S‖θ‖ₑ, so this is the density hypothesis of tangent_locality
tangent_locality with (M, θ) and (E, θ) at x gives the equivalence for every Q

subproblems.title: Changing the multiplicity on a set of locally finite measure preserves weighted approximate tangent spaces almost everywhere
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ and H := μHE[k] on ℝ^N = Eucl N. Let E ⊆ ℝ^N be H-null-measurable with H(E ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N, and let θ, θ′ : ℝ^N → ℝ both be H-integrable on E ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N, with θ > 0 on E (no sign condition on θ′). Then for H-a.e. x ∈ E (H⌞E-almost every x) and every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^N: if Q is a weighted approximate tangent space of (E, θ) at x (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.7), then Q is a weighted approximate tangent space of (E, θ′) at x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (E : Set (Eucl N)) (θ θ' : Eucl N → ℝ), NullMeasurableSet E (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N)) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl N), IsCompact K → (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N)) (E ∩ K) < ∞) → (∀ x ∈ E, 0 < θ x) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl N), IsCompact K → IntegrableOn θ (E ∩ K) (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N))) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl N), IsCompact K → IntegrableOn θ' (E ∩ K) (μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N))) → ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[k] : Measure (Eucl N)).restrict E), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Eucl N), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ' x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the weight lemma of the parent proof (its Lemma 2, Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1)): on a set with locally finite Hᵏ measure the approximate tangent space does not depend on the positive multiplicity. Weight 1 is the unweighted Definition 1.4, so θ′ ≡ 1 or θ ≡ 1 gives the two directions of that Lemma 2. The parent proof uses Lusin's theorem and continuity on compact pieces. Here the same comparison uses normalized Lebesgue points, which are the reused sibling lebesgue_points (Submission.iwl_imc_normalized_lebesgue_points, statement (LP)), together with the reused sibling tangent_locality ((TL), as stated in subset_locality). Notation as in subset_locality: ‖t‖ₑ = |t|, B̄_ρ(x) := closedBall x ρ, r^{−k} := ENNReal.ofReal((r^k)⁻¹).

(LP) [sibling lebesgue_points, used with U := ℝ^N]: if E ⊆ ℝ^N is H-null-measurable, H(E ∩ K) < ∞ and f : ℝ^N → ℝ is H-integrable on E ∩ K for every compact K, then for H⌞E-a.e. x and every R > 0, r^{−k}·∫⁻_{E∩B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖f(y) − f(x)‖ₑ dH(y) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
(TL) [sibling tangent_locality]: for H-null-measurable M, M′, functions θ, θ′ and a point x with θ(x) = θ′(x), suppose that for some ρ > 0 θ is integrable on M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) and θ′ on M′ ∩ B̄_ρ(x), and that r^{−k}·∫⁻_{B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖1_Mθ − 1_{M′}θ′‖ₑ dH → 0 as r ↓ 0 for every R > 0. Then HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x Q ↔ HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M′ θ′ x Q for every Q.

1. (Good points.)
   - Apply (LP) to f := θ and to f := θ′. The hypotheses are E null-measurable, H(E ∩ K) < ∞, and integrability of θ, θ′ on E ∩ K; the conditions K ⊆ ℝ^N and E ⊆ ℝ^N are automatic.
   - Intersect the two H⌞E-a.e. statements with x ∈ E (ae_restrict_mem₀). Then H⌞E-a.e. x satisfies x ∈ E and, for every R > 0, as r ↓ 0:
     A(r) := r^{−k}·∫⁻_{E∩B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖θ(y) − θ(x)‖ₑ dH(y) → 0,
     A′(r) := r^{−k}·∫⁻_{E∩B̄_{Rr}(x)} ‖θ′(y) − θ′(x)‖ₑ dH(y) → 0.
   Fix such an x and a linear subspace Q with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ x Q.

2. (Normalizing constant.) θ(x) > 0 because x ∈ E. Put c := θ′(x)/θ(x) and θ̃(y) := c·θ(y). Then θ̃(x) = c·θ(x) = θ′(x).

3. (Homogeneity of Definition 1.7.) HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ̃ x Q holds.
   - finrank Q = k is unchanged.
   - For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) and every r, ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} f(y)·θ̃(x + ry) dH(y) = c·∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} f(y)·θ(x + ry) dH(y). This is integral_const_mul, valid for every integrand (both sides vanish together if the integrand is not integrable).
   - By hypothesis the right side tends to c·θ(x)·∫_Q f dH = θ̃(x)·∫_Q f dH as r ↓ 0.

4. (Density estimate.) Fix R > 0 and r ∈ ℝ, and write B := B̄_{Rr}(x).
   - For z ∈ E, c·θ(x) = θ′(x) gives θ̃(z) − θ′(z) = c(θ(z) − θ(x)) − (θ′(z) − θ′(x)). Hence ‖θ̃(z) − θ′(z)‖ₑ ≤ ‖c‖ₑ·‖θ(z) − θ(x)‖ₑ + ‖θ′(z) − θ′(x)‖ₑ.
   - ‖1_Eθ̃(z) − 1_Eθ′(z)‖ₑ = 1_E(z)·‖θ̃(z) − θ′(z)‖ₑ, and E is null-measurable for H⌞B. As in step 4 of subset_locality, ∫⁻_B ‖1_Eθ̃ − 1_Eθ′‖ₑ dH = ∫⁻_{E∩B} ‖θ̃ − θ′‖ₑ dH.
   - Integrate the pointwise bound over E ∩ B. Then ∫⁻_{E∩B} ‖θ̃ − θ′‖ₑ dH ≤ ‖c‖ₑ·∫⁻_{E∩B} ‖θ − θ(x)‖ₑ dH + ∫⁻_{E∩B} ‖θ′ − θ′(x)‖ₑ dH.
     · The integral of the sum splits (lintegral_add_left′), because y ↦ ‖c‖ₑ·‖θ(y) − θ(x)‖ₑ is a.e.-measurable for H⌞(E ∩ B): θ is integrable on E ∩ B (the integrability hypothesis with the compact set K := B).
     · The constant ‖c‖ₑ < ∞ is pulled out by lintegral_const_mul′.
   - Multiply by r^{−k}: 0 ≤ r^{−k}·∫⁻_B ‖1_Eθ̃ − 1_Eθ′‖ₑ dH ≤ ‖c‖ₑ·A(r) + A′(r).
   - By step 1 the right side tends to ‖c‖ₑ·0 + 0 = 0 as r ↓ 0 (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul, Tendsto.add). By squeezing, so does the middle term, for every R > 0.

5. (Apply (TL).) Use (TL) with (M, θ) := (E, θ̃), (M′, θ′) := (E, θ′) and the point x:
   - E is H-null-measurable, and θ̃(x) = θ′(x) by step 2;
   - with ρ := 1, θ̃ = cθ and θ′ are integrable on E ∩ B̄_1(x) (the integrability hypotheses with the compact set K := B̄_1(x), and Integrable.const_mul);
   - the density hypothesis is step 4.
   Hence HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ̃ x Q ↔ HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k E θ′ x Q, and step 3 gives the left side. So Q is a weighted approximate tangent space of (E, θ′) at x. This holds for H⌞E-a.e. x and every Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: lebesgue_points for θ and θ′ on E: r^{−k}·∫⁻_{E∩B̄_{Rr}(x)} |θ − θ(x)| dH → 0 and likewise for θ′, H⌞E-a.e.
c := θ′(x)/θ(x); homogeneity of Definition 1.7: HasWATS(E, θ, x, Q) implies HasWATS(E, cθ, x, Q)
tangent_locality with (E, cθ) and (E, θ′), using cθ(x) = θ′(x)

subproblems.title: Weighted approximate tangent spaces of two carriers agree almost everywhere on their overlap
subproblems.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ and H := μHE[k] on ℝ^N = Eucl N. Let M₁, M₂ ⊆ ℝ^N be H-null-measurable and let θ₁, θ₂ : ℝ^N → ℝ satisfy θ_i > 0 on M_i and θ_i H-integrable on M_i ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N (i = 1, 2). Then for H-a.e. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ (H⌞(M₁ ∩ M₂)-almost every x) and every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^N: if Q is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M₁, θ₁) at x (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M₁ θ₁ x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.7), then Q is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M₂, θ₂) at x.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Corollary 3 of the parent proof and the tangent-space transfer chains of its Steps 4 and 7. The parent's chain HasWATS(M₁, θ₁) ⇒ tangent space of M₁ ⇒ of M₁ ∩ M₂ ⇒ of M₂ ⇒ HasWATS(M₂, θ₂) uses Lemma 2, Lemma 1, Lemma 1, Lemma 2. Here it runs with the weighted siblings subset_locality (Lemma 1) and weight_change (Lemma 2). Two things differ from the parent's Corollary 3:
   - The reused im_combine needs this comparison for all positive multiplicities, not only integer ones.
   - Lemma 2 needs locally finite Hᵏ measure. So the overlap is first cut into the pieces E_j on which both multiplicities are ≥ 1/(j+1). This is the device of Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1), whose compact pieces M_j carry a positive lower bound for θ.
HasWATS(A, ϑ, x, Q) abbreviates HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k A ϑ x Q, and B̄_m(0) := closedBall 0 m.

1. (θ_i is a.e.-measurable on M_i.) Fix i.
   - ℝ^N = ⋃_{m∈ℕ} B̄_m(0) (iUnion_closedBall_nat), so M_i = ⋃_m (M_i ∩ B̄_m(0)).
   - B̄_m(0) is compact, so θ_i is integrable, hence a.e.-strongly measurable, on each M_i ∩ B̄_m(0).
   - By countable gluing (aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff), θ_i is a.e.-strongly measurable for H⌞M_i.

2. (Superlevel sets.) For t ∈ ℝ, M_i ∩ {θ_i ≥ t} is H-null-measurable.
   - By step 1 choose a strongly measurable g with θ_i = g H⌞M_i-a.e.
   - M_i is null-measurable, so ae_restrict_iff′₀ gives: for H-a.e. y, y ∈ M_i implies θ_i(y) = g(y).
   - Hence M_i ∩ {θ_i ≥ t} and M_i ∩ {g ≥ t} agree outside an H-null set. The latter is null-measurable (null-measurable ∩ measurable), so the former is too (NullMeasurableSet.congr).

3. (Truncated overlaps.) For j ∈ ℕ let c_j := 1/(j+1) > 0 and E_j := (M₁ ∩ {θ₁ ≥ c_j}) ∩ (M₂ ∩ {θ₂ ≥ c_j}).
   - Each E_j is H-null-measurable (step 2) and E_j ⊆ M₁ ∩ M₂.
   - Conversely, let y ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂. Then min(θ₁(y), θ₂(y)) > 0, so some j has 1/(j+1) < min(θ₁(y), θ₂(y)) (exists_nat_one_div_lt), i.e. y ∈ E_j.
   - Hence M₁ ∩ M₂ = ⋃_j E_j.

4. (Hᵏ⌞E_j is locally finite.) Let K be compact. On E_j ∩ K we have ofReal θ₁ ≥ ofReal c_j, and E_j ∩ K is null-measurable. Hence
   ofReal(c_j)·H(E_j ∩ K) = ∫⁻_{E_j∩K} ofReal(c_j) dH ≤ ∫⁻_{E_j∩K} ofReal(θ₁) dH ≤ ∫⁻_{M₁∩K} ofReal(θ₁) dH < ∞,
   by setLIntegral_const, lintegral_mono_ae with ae_restrict_mem₀, lintegral_mono_set, and integrability of θ₁ on M₁ ∩ K. Since ofReal(c_j) > 0, H(E_j ∩ K) < ∞ (ENNReal.mul_lt_top_iff).

5. (Comparison on E_j.) Fix j. Then θ₁ > 0 on E_j, and for every compact K the sets E_j ∩ K ⊆ M_i ∩ K carry integrable θ_i (IntegrableOn.mono_set). Apply:
   (a) subset_locality to E_j ⊆ M₁ with θ₁: H⌞E_j-a.e., HasWATS(M₁, θ₁, x, Q) ↔ HasWATS(E_j, θ₁, x, Q) for every Q;
   (b) weight_change to E_j with (θ, θ′) := (θ₁, θ₂), using step 4 for H(E_j ∩ K) < ∞: H⌞E_j-a.e., HasWATS(E_j, θ₁, x, Q) → HasWATS(E_j, θ₂, x, Q) for every Q;
   (c) subset_locality to E_j ⊆ M₂ with θ₂: H⌞E_j-a.e., HasWATS(M₂, θ₂, x, Q) ↔ HasWATS(E_j, θ₂, x, Q) for every Q.
   Intersect the three a.e. statements. For H⌞E_j-a.e. x and every Q:
   HasWATS(M₁, θ₁, x, Q) ⇒ (a) HasWATS(E_j, θ₁, x, Q) ⇒ (b) HasWATS(E_j, θ₂, x, Q) ⇒ (c) HasWATS(M₂, θ₂, x, Q).

6. (Countable union.)
   - By step 3, H⌞(M₁ ∩ M₂) = H⌞(⋃_j E_j).
   - A property holds H⌞(⋃_j E_j)-a.e. iff it holds H⌞E_j-a.e. for every j (ae_restrict_iUnion_iff, countable index set ℕ).
   - Step 5 gives the latter, which proves the claim. ∎
